newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Senate balance unchanged by death.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Senate balance unchanged by death.

text.p: The death of Australian government senator John Panizza would not affect the balance of power in the upper house of parliament, the Australian Opposition said on Friday.

A spokesman for Senate Opposition Leader John Faulkner told Reuters that the Labor Party would give up one of its votes for the loss of Panizza's, thus maintaining the current balance of power in the non-government dominated Senate.
"John (Faulkner) thinks that's the best thing to do under the circumstances," the spokesman told Reuters.
Panizza, 65, died in his sleep on Thursday night, while on parliamentary business in the Queensland town of Cairns.
The Western Australian senator, who was elected to parliament in 1987, was government whip in the Senate and was the first person of Italian parentage ever elected to the upper house.
Prime Minister John Howard said Panizza would be sadly missed.
"Senator Panizza was a tireless worker for the people of Western Australia and a great worker for the Liberal Party," Howard said in a statement.
